title: Team and product: talking about people and things
theme: Команда и продукт: кто что делает, что в продукте есть и чего не хватает
can_do: Описать команду: сколько людей, кто чем занимается, как делят работу.
Правильно ставить a, the или ничего перед существительным в рассказе о работе.
Не терять -s: three features, every task, she works, there are two bugs.
Говорить о количестве: much, many, a lot of, a few, most, both, the whole.
Ответить на вопрос собеседования о приоритетах в бэклоге.

points.title: a / an, the or no article
points.explain_ru: a/an ставят, когда предмет один из многих или появляется впервые: We hired a designer. the ставят, когда понятно, какой именно: его уже называли, он один в этой ситуации или его уточнили (the designer we hired, the CEO, the report you sent). Без артикля говорят о многих вообще и о неисчисляемом: Users hate long forms. Feedback matters. Помогает вопрос: знает ли собеседник, о каком именно речь? Знает: the. Любой из многих: a. Все вообще: ничего.

examples.ru: В прошлом месяце мы наняли нового дизайнера. Дизайнер уже переделал онбординг.

ru_trap.wrong: Yesterday I had meeting with new client.
ru_trap.right: Yesterday I had a meeting with a new client.
ru_trap.why_ru: В русском артиклей нет, поэтому перед "встреча" и "клиент" ничего не ставится. В английском исчисляемое слово в единственном числе почти никогда не стоит голым: нужен a, the или my, this.

points.title: Uncountable nouns: advice, information, feedback
points.explain_ru: Некоторые слова в английском неисчисляемые, хотя по-русски их можно посчитать: advice, information, feedback, news, research, equipment, software, progress, knowledge, work (в значении "работа"). С ними нет a/an и нет -s, а глагол стоит в единственном числе: The feedback was positive. Чтобы посчитать, нужен кусок: a piece of advice, two pieces of feedback. Вместо many с ними ставят much, вместо a few ставят a little.

examples.en: Thanks for the feedback, it was really useful.

examples.en: We need to do some research before we start.

ru_trap.why_ru: По-русски "советы" бывают во множественном числе. В английском advice неисчисляемое: без -s и без a. Один совет: a piece of advice.

points.title: Plural -s; every and each + singular
points.explain_ru: Если предметов больше одного, у существительного -s, даже когда количество уже понятно из числа или слова: three projects, many users, all my tasks, a lot of ideas. После every и each наоборот: существительное в единственном числе и глагол с -s: every task has an owner, each team member gets a laptop. Every значит "каждый из всех", но грамматически это один предмет. Неправильные формы запомнить: person - people, child - children.

examples.en: We released three new features last quarter.

examples.en: Every task needs an owner and a deadline.

examples.en: A lot of users asked for a dark mode.

ru_trap.wrong: Every sprints ends with a demo.
ru_trap.right: Every sprint ends with a demo.
ru_trap.why_ru: По-русски "все спринты" и "каждый спринт" близки по смыслу, и -s переносится на every. В английском после every и each всегда одно: every sprint, each user.

points.title: Verb -s: she works, there is / there are
points.explain_ru: В настоящем времени после he, she, it и любого одного лица или предмета (my manager, the app, everyone, nobody) глагол получает -s: she works, the app crashes, everyone knows. В вопросе и отрицании -s переходит в does/doesn't, а глагол остается без -s: Does it work? It doesn't work. There is + один предмет или неисчисляемое (there is a bug, there is some feedback), there are + много (there are two bugs). Слово team в британском варианте может идти и с are: the team are happy; оба варианта верны.

ru_trap.why_ru: В русском окончание глагола меняется у всех лиц, а в английском почти никогда, поэтому -s кажется лишним. Но это единственный след третьего лица: he works, she doesn't.

points.title: much, many, a few, most, both, the whole
points.explain_ru: Сколько: many и a few с исчисляемыми (many users, a few bugs), much и a little с неисчисляемыми (much time, a little feedback). В утверждениях вместо much и many обычно говорят a lot of: We have a lot of work. Few и little без a значат "мало, и это плохо": Few people came. Определители: most + существительное о всех вообще (most users), most of the + конкретная группа (most of the users we interviewed), both о двух (both options), the whole + единственное число (the whole team), all the + конкретная группа (all the tests).

examples.en: We don't have much time, but we have a lot of ideas.
examples.ru: Времени у нас мало, а идей много.

examples.en: Most users never open the settings page.
examples.ru: Большинство пользователей никогда не открывают настройки.

examples.en: Most of the people we interviewed wanted a mobile app.
examples.ru: Большинство опрошенных хотели мобильное приложение.

examples.en: Both options have risks, so let's compare them.
examples.ru: У обоих вариантов есть риски, давай их сравним.

examples.en: The whole team worked on the release, and all the tests passed.
examples.ru: Вся команда работала над релизом, и все тесты прошли.

ru_trap.wrong: Most of users like the new design.
ru_trap.right: Most users like the new design.
ru_trap.why_ru: Русское "большинство пользователей" тянет за собой of. Most of нужен только перед the, my, these и местоимениями: most of the users we asked, most of them.

article_card.rule_ru: Новый предмет в рассказе вводи через a/an. Когда он уже назван, это "тот самый": the. Без артикля говорят о многих вообще и о неисчисляемом.

reading.title: A month without a manager
reading.text:
Brightline is a small company that makes an app for local food markets. There are eleven people in the product team: five developers, two testers, a designer, a data analyst, a product manager and a support specialist. Every person on the team has a clear area, but nobody works alone.

Every Monday the team meets for thirty minutes. The product manager, Ines, brings the latest feedback from customers, and the team decides which problems to solve first. Most of the feedback is about small things: a button that is hard to find, a slow page, a confusing message. A few requests are bigger, and those go to the backlog.

Last spring the team tried something new. For one month there was no manager in the room. Each developer talked to customers directly, and the testers wrote the release notes. The experiment was useful, but it wasn't easy. Some people loved the freedom. Others said they spent too much time in meetings and didn't have enough time for real work.

In the end the team kept one idea from the experiment: every developer spends one hour a week reading customer messages. "It changed how we write code," says Tomas, one of the developers. "When you read the same complaint ten times, nobody needs to explain the priority to you."

Today the whole team still meets on Mondays, but the meeting is shorter. There is less discussion and there are more decisions.

listening.title: No more bosses (Episode 200806, 06 Aug 2020)

questions.q: How do Neil and Georgina describe their own working relationship?
questions.answer: It is good; Georgina says they make a great team.
A system of organising people according to their level of importance: managers on top, workers below.

questions.q: Which company was one of the first to try self-management, and what does it do?
questions.answer: Morning Star, a tomato grower in California.

questions.q: What two principles does Doug Kirkpatrick describe?
questions.answer: People should not use force or coercion against each other, and people should keep the commitments they make to each other.

questions.q: What is the possible downside of having no bosses?
questions.answer: Extra responsibility can mean more work and stress, and some employees may be left behind.

questions.q: How much do excess management and bureaucracy cost the US economy every year?

key_points: Many people have had a bad boss, often because workers feel managers don't listen to them.
Most companies are hierarchies, with managers on top and workers below.
At Morning Star there are no bosses: nobody can force others, and everyone must keep their commitments.
Some employees take full advantage of self-management, others may be left behind.
Everyone is still held accountable for their work.
Excess management and bureaucracy cost the US economy about 3 trillion dollars a year.
